$comment: Maintainer ruling 2026-09-12: Copilot supplies the sole automated review round. A separate APPROVED review is not required; the maintainer's human merge decision remains outside this automated readiness verdict. AUDITED 2026-09-18 -- this file is VALID at nen 0.10.0 and the empty default_approvers is DELIBERATE, said here rather than by omission, which is exactly what the loader demands. `approval_policy: "review-round-only"` is NOT inert: it is the key that makes the empty approval set legal, and it is load-bearing in both directions. Measured against the installed 0.10.0 binary: `nen schema check --repo .` reports `ok nen/gates.json`, and `nen pr ready <n> --gh-repo zheref/hatsu` evaluates normally (#76 -> not-ready, a reviewer round still owed at head). DELETE `approval_policy` and the same loader refuses: `at default_approvers, is empty. An empty approval set makes the approve limb of the readiness gate VACUOUSLY TRUE ...`. Set it to anything else and it refuses too: `at approval_policy, expected 'required' or 'review-round-only'`. A grep finding no consumer for `review-round-only` in a zheref/nen source tree means that CHECKOUT predates the feature -- it landed in nen 0.10.0 (nen #209, PR #210; release PR #211), which is why nen/contract.json raises `minimum` to 0.10. Check the checkout version before reading an absence as evidence. So: do not "fix" this file by populating default_approvers, and do not remove approval_policy as dead configuration. Doing either changes the readiness verdict for every Hatsu pull request.

delivery.$comment: Current local delivery branches use the Codex prefix and the maintainer credentials.

round_policy.$comment: Maintainer's rulings of 2026-09-19 (zheref/hatsu#85). stallMinutes is read by nen pr ready (v0.11.0): a pending review request older than it reads not-ready: reviewer round stalled. minRounds and maxRounds are Hatsu's own keys, read by the skills: an owed reviewer round is requested on the maintainer's behalf while the PR's requested rounds are under maxRounds; at maxRounds the run ends at not-ready with the board, never with a question. monitor.maxCycles in nen/workflow.json is a different number -- en's ACTING-cycle cap.
